statements.t: “We delivered third quarter results that came in above guidance, all while continuing to strengthen our commercial capabilities, improve operating efficiency and enhance the guest experience,” said John W.
We are seeing the early signs of progress and expect Net Yield growth of 1% to 2% in 2027, with a meaningful acceleration in the back half of the year.”
The Company delivered third quarter results above guidance, driven primarily by stronger-than-expected close-in demand and onboard spend.
Reflecting its stronger-than-expected third quarter performance, the Company is raising its full year 2026 guidance.

The expanded offering at Great Stirrup Cay, including the recently opened Great Tides Waterpark, together with the upcoming rollout of a new marketing platform and improvements to revenue management capabilities, including the implementation of the base-loading strategy across 2027 and 2028 sailings, is expected to support stronger demand and a healthier booking curve over time.

These trends, together with the expected benefits of the Company’s commercial initiatives, support the Company’s expectation for full year Net Yield growth of 1% to 2%, with a meaningful acceleration in the second half.
We continue to center our focus on cost discipline and cash generation as we work to restore Net Yield growth, with stronger earnings and cash flow expected to drive further deleveraging.”

In addition to announcing the results for the third quarter of 2026, the Company also provided guidance for the fourth quarter and full year 2026, along with accompanying sensitivities, subject to changes in the broad macroeconomic environment.
The Company has not provided reconciliations between the Company’s 2026 guidance and the most directly comparable GAAP measures because it would be too difficult to prepare a reliable U.S.
The following reflects the foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026 that the Company used in its fourth quarter and full year 2026 guidance.
As of October 15, 2026, the Company had hedged approximately 48% and 42% of its total projected metric tons of fuel consumption for 2026 and 2027, respectively.
Our presentation of our non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed as an inference that our future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items.
